source_rationale: This label represents superficial lamina propria fibroblasts that are ADAMDEC1+, ABCA8+, FABP4+ and form the dominant fibroblast population across datasets and samples. FOS+ Fibroblast Lamina propria or Ribo(high) Fibroblast Lamina propria, and note an upper-lamina WNT4+ subset (Stroma_0_2) described in the literature, as well as plasma (IGHA+) and myeloid (C1S/C1R+) doublet-contaminated clusters. Taken together, the transcriptional program, high dataset and sample diversity, and literature on WNT4+ villus-oriented fibroblasts support a high-confidence lamina propria fibroblast identity, with FOS and ribosomal signatures reflecting activation state rather than separate cell types.

source_rationale: S2A fibroblasts sit near the crypt base and are enriched for VSTM2A together with PDGFRA, BMP4, WNT5A, POSTN and other S2 markers. Several clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Bottom (S2A) show very low dataset diversity but reproducible expression of POSTN, F3 and BMPs, and differences between individual S2A annotation clusters are subtle (see annotation_cluster) and may largely reflect activation and quality flags (for example high mitochondrial content) rather than true subtypes. We therefore annotate a single S2A cell type corresponding to crypt-bottom fibroblasts with high-confidence positional identity and variable activation signatures.

source_rationale: S2B fibroblasts are positioned toward the crypt top or villus tip and are characterized by NRG1 and NPY, we also highlight VEGFD and TRPA1 as convincing markers of villus-tip subepithelial fibroblasts. Clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Top (S2B) (for example Stroma_1_1 and 12_1–12_4) show these markers along with the broader S2 program and are present in multiple datasets, albeit with varying mitochondrial content and dataset diversity. We therefore treat S2B as a robust positional subtype of S2, capturing villus-tip fibroblasts with strong NRG1/VEGFD/TRPA1 signatures.

source_rationale: This label captures glia associated with the muscularis propria that show markers such as SLC5A7, APOD and KCNS3 in addition to a core glial program. These clusters are enriched in full-thickness specimens with abundant muscle, and rare or absent in superficial biopsies, consistent with a muscularis propria localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes
